newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON AND BUTCHER ENSURE DRAW FOR ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON AND BUTCHER ENSURE DRAW FOR ENGLAND.

text.p: Michael Atherton and Mark Butcher shared an opening partnership of 162 on Monday to ensure a draw for England in the rain-shortened second Ashes test against Australia at Lord's.

Shane Warne, relishing the sun on his back for the first time in the match, created some tremors in the England dressing room when he dismissed Butcher (87) and Nasser Hussain (nought) in successive overs.

But Graham Thorpe (30 not out) and John Crawley (29 not out) survived the mini-crisis and when play was finally called off on the fifth and final day, England were 266 for four, a considerable advance on their first innings 77. Australia declared their first innings closed at the overnight total of 213 for seven.
On a pitch lacking the demons of the previous days, Atherton and Butcher saw off man-of-the-match Glenn McGrath, who had destroyed their first innings with eight for 38.
The England captain, still to get a first-class century at cricket's headquarters, struck 10 boundaries in scoring 77, his 33rd test half-century.
Butcher, playing for his test place, survived a chance at first slip to Taylor off Paul Reiffel when he had scored only two.

He was given a searching examination outside the off-stump by the Austrlaian pacemen but fought on to reach his maiden test half-century. When he was finally bowled out of the bowlers' rough by Warne, the Surrey left-hander had batted for 265 minutes and hit 14 fours from 210 balls.
England retained their 1-0 lead in the six-test series after the nine-wicket victory at Edgbaston while the draw was Australia's first after 18 previous tests had finished in a definite result.
